title: ACS 2025 1-year estimates: eight headline indicators for every state, DC and the US
sealed_at_note: written by our own machine; the independent date is the OpenTimestamps proof acs-2025-seal.json.ots

target.release_basis: announced: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/news/data-releases/2025/release-schedule.html ('Data will be released on October 29'; schedule row 'October 29, 2026', 1-Year Data Release, products include Data Profiles, Detailed Tables and Summary File)
target.summary_file_due: announced: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/news/data-releases/2025/release.html ('The 1-year Summary File on the FTP site will be available on release day.')

vintage.note: ACS 1-year estimates are published once and not revised; Census corrects errors by errata notes. The value scored is the one released 2026-10-29; a later erratum is reported beside the score, not scored.

routes.primary: the 2025 table-based summary file (acsdt1y2025-<table>.dat) fetched on or after 2026-10-29, lines mapped by label from ACS20251YR_Table_Shells.txt, computed and rounded exactly as the history
routes.fallback: if the summary file is not posted on 2026-10-29: the 2025 data-profile value (variable mapped by label from the 2025 profile variables.json) read from data.census.gov's api/access/data/table endpoint that day
routes.agreement_2024: the two routes give identical values for all 8 indicators and 52 geographies in 2024 (416 of 416), checked 2026-10-27

scoring.rounding: shares in percent to one decimal and medians in whole dollars, rounded half away from zero, as the data profiles print them
scoring.metric: absolute error per indicator and geography for every sealed method (the served method is the headline; the random walk and drift are the baselines); the mean over the 51 states, the US scored on its own; whether each value falls inside each method's sealed 80% and 95% bands

model.selection_rule: Serve the method with the lowest pooled out-of-time MAE over the backtest targets. Where the ensemble's MAE gap to that method has a 95% interval (target years resampled) that holds zero, serve the ensemble. If the method served is the random walk, the indicator is not sealed: the model adds nothing over repeating last year.
model.bands: every method gets its own 80% and 95% band: studentized split-conformal from one-year-ahead backtest residuals pooled across the 52 geographies (factor = the conformal quantile of |residual| / scale; scale = the geography's spread of year-to-year changes, shrunk toward the panel median with two pseudo-observations)
model.sealed: every method's point and bands are sealed; the served method is the headline

caveats: The 2025 collection year included a federal shutdown (October 1 to November 12, 2025), and the release came later than the usual mid-September. Neither Census's 2025 release schedule nor its 'New and Notable' page mentions the shutdown, interrupted collection or affected estimates (both read 2026-10-27), and no 2025 user note names an affected indicator, so none is marked affected. The bands come from past one-year-ahead misses and cannot capture a collection or processing break in 2025.

Median gross rent: from the 2024 data Census raised the contract-rent cap to $20,000 a month (user note 2025-06, https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/user-notes/2025-06.html). Medians move little, but 2024 is not like-for-like with earlier years.
Backtest targets skip 2020 and 2021: 2020 has no standard release, and 2019 to 2021 is a two-year step, so one-year-ahead residuals come from 2017-2019 and 2022-2024 (2019, 2022-2024 for broadband).
Dollar indicators are nominal (each survey year's own dollars), as the data profiles print them.
claim_rule: 'sealed before publication' only if the OpenTimestamps attestation's block time precedes 2026-10-29; a seal attested on or after the release is void
